learning: Iteration 6 showed that the narrower track raised slalom line loss to 0.35 at kp 3.0. Turn gain scales with kp/wheel_track, so kp 2.5 restores the iteration-5 effective gain. If line loss stays at 0.2 or higher, the track, not the gain, is the cause, and I will ask for wheel_track 0.12 again.
notes: Holds the iteration-6 geometry (wheel_track 0.10) as the Builder requested, and reduces kp from 3.0 to 2.5 to match the effective turn gain of the iteration-5 platform. This isolates the gain change on the narrower track.
rationale: Iteration 6 (wheel_track 0.10, kp 3.0) scored 72.91, down from 111.80. Slalom line loss rose to 0.35 per run, and oval progress fell from 0.55 to 0.28. max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.064 m on all tracks, so the narrower track did not solve tracking. The Builder's rule and my own earlier feedback both call for a gain reduction when slalom line loss is 0.2 or higher, and I am following that rule. The geometry is held exactly as iteration 6: five sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.10, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12, body_length 0.18, mass 0.8. Turn rate per unit of wheel differential scales as 1/wheel_track, so moving from 0.12 to 0.10 m raised effective loop gain by about 20 percent. To hold effective gain at the iteration-5 level, which had slalom line loss 0.10, I scale kp by the track ratio: kp = 3.0 x 0.10/0.12, which is 2.5. ki stays at 0.05 and kd at 0.3 to keep the damping unchanged, and base_speed stays at 1.2 and line_loss stays last_direction, since neither was implicated. Expected result, not measured: slalom line loss back toward 0.1 or below, and oval progress recovering toward 0.4 to 0.5. max_error may stay near 0.063 m, which would indicate gain balance is the remaining limit rather than geometry.
